source.title: A Capacity Scaling Law for Artificial Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including sections, conclusion, references and appended code; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper empirically measures how often MLPs fit randomly generated inputs with different labelings to estimate lossless-memory and MacKay dimensions. This bears on fitting random labels, but it measures capacity boundaries rather than the original image-classification intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper's results concern capacity measurements on randomly generated data and labelings. Its discussion of Zhang et al. [44] and Arpit et al. [2] is cited prior work and is not extracted as this study's result. Figure-only capacity curves are not assigned numerical rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures capacity boundaries of small MLPs on generated points, primarily using L-BFGS and repeated optimization attempts. It does not establish random-label fitting or failure in the standard deep networks and unchanged stochastic-training setting named by V1. Its capacity bounds do not contradict fitting datasets within capacity. The original randomization experiments are discussed as prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion. More precisely, they claim linear upper bounds for lossless-memory and MacKay capacity in parameter count, report experiments consistent with those bounds, and propose capacity measurement as a task-independent implementation benchmark. They emphasize that practical effectiveness varies substantially and falls below their theoretical bounds.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures capacity by sampling low-dimensional random points and testing possible labelings, rather than reproducing random-label image-classification experiments. It uses scikit-learn MLPs, primarily with L-BFGS, and also tests other optimizers, implementations and activations.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer and implementation (L-BFGS versus Adam/SGD and scikit-learn versus Keras); input data distribution (uniform versus normal); activation function; network depth and dimensions.

fits_no_version.finding: Small MLPs fit arbitrary binary labelings up to empirically measured capacity boundaries; capacity varies with optimizer, activation, input distribution, and depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Empirical random-point shattering capacity depends on network size and implementation, with approximately linear scaling in the tested configurations.

record.problems: Empirical tests sample rather than exhaust all labelings above 15 samples (up to 2^15), and MK tests are capped at 10 samples. The authors note the theoretical bounds are upper bounds and practical implementations fall below them. Optimizer and implementation strongly affect fitting; figures contain many detailed values not stated in prose.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-configuration numerical values in Figure 2 and characteristic curves in Figure 3 are figure-only; no precise values were reconstructed. Cited results attributed to Zhang et al. [44] and Arpit et al. [2] were excluded because they are prior work, not this paper's own experiments.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting by standard deep networks with stochastic training, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance test performance.
Training-time comparison between true and random labels, and convergence as label corruption increases.
Zero training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs using the same networks.
Training and test error across a label-corruption sweep.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noise.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text is sufficient for this assessment. Missing claim components are untested, rather than evidence limiting a version. The record also misstates the MK computational cap: the text describes a cap on tested labelings, not a maximum of 10 data samples. Both appended procedures select the best outcome across datasets and optimization restarts, which matters when interpreting the capacity estimates.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test random labelings of training images, report test error at chance, compare to true-label generalization, or establish unchanged hyperparameters against an image-classification baseline.
Does not compare training time for true and random labels or measure convergence slowdown as label corruption increases.
Does not test shuffled, permuted or Gaussian-noise image inputs; its normally distributed inputs are low-dimensional generated points for capacity measurement.
Does not sweep a fraction of corrupted labels while measuring training and test error.
Does not test the effects of weight decay, dropout or data augmentation on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Does not compare learning over time for real versus random labels.

rows.subject: MLP implementation in scikit-learn
rows.operation_detail: Measured the empirical LM dimension by increasing randomly generated sample count and testing labelings for fit.

conditions.value: all labelings where feasible; random selection of 2^15 labelings above 15 samples

rows.measure: Empirical VC/LM dimension: largest sample count for which all tested labelings were fitted.
rows.value: The paper states that one hidden neuron behaves like a single perceptron with LM dimension k + 1; no per-k empirical numerical values stated in text.
rows.note: The text reports the 1-hidden-neuron relation but does not provide the empirical per-dimension values in text; the figure contains the detailed curves.
rows.check: A one-hidden-neuron capacity result under L-BFGS does not measure V1's standard deep-network behavior. The text states the k + 1 relationship, but supplies no individual empirical values.

rows.subject: MLP implementation in scikit-learn
rows.size_stated: hidden nodes h = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]; input dimensions k = [1, 2, 3, 4]
rows.operation_detail: Measured how many randomly generated sample points could be shattered by testing their labelings.

conditions.value: up to 2^15; above 15 samples, random selection of 2^15

rows.measure: Empirical LM/VC dimension, the sample count at which not all possible labelings could be fitted.
rows.value: Empirical VC dimensions come quite close to h k + 1 for small numbers; a few cases for 2 hidden nodes and input dimensions 3, 4, or 5 shattered 9, 11, or 13 samples, respectively.
rows.note: The paper uses random points and labelings, and reports capacity results; it does not report zero training error on a fixed image training set with chance test error.
rows.check: Small shallow-network shattering capacity under L-BFGS does not establish V1. The exceptional 9-, 11-, and 13-sample results are selected dataset examples, not guaranteed capacity across datasets. The exceptional cases include input dimension 5 despite the stated main sweep ending at 4.

rows.subject: MLP implementation in scikit-learn
rows.operation_detail: Compared empirical capacity across optimizers while attempting to fit randomly labeled generated data.
rows.measure: Ability to fit the tested random labelings / resulting measured dimensions.
rows.baseline: L-BFGS, with which the paper reports better fitting
rows.value: In most cases, the net was not able to fit the data in contrast to using L-BFGS; measured dimensions were very low.
rows.note: The reported optimizer comparison is a direct qualification: the capacity result depends on optimizer and implementation.
rows.check: The qualitative optimizer comparison does not specify architectures, sample counts relative to capacity, or separate Adam, SGD, and Keras outcomes. Failure in these small capacity experiments cannot establish absence of V1 in standard deep networks.

rows.subject: MLP implementation in scikit-learn
rows.operation_detail: Measured ability to fit random labelings while changing data distribution.
rows.value: Changing it to sampling from a normal distribution improved our results dramatically.
rows.note: The paper explicitly says generated data distribution materially changed measured capacity.
rows.check: This measures a distribution-dependent change in estimated capacity, without reporting V1's behavior under its specified training conditions. Normally distributed low-dimensional points also do not establish V3 for the same networks used in the original experiments.

rows.subject: MLP implementation in scikit-learn
rows.operation_detail: Measured capacity with different gating functions on random generated data.
rows.value: With identity, the network mostly behaved like a single perceptron; tanh and logistic results looked similar to ReLU but needed more repetitions and processing time.
rows.locator: Section 5, Tuning the Implementation; Section 6, Conclusion
rows.note: Different activations were tested, with different computational effort reported.
rows.check: This combines different activation conditions into a qualitative capacity comparison. Extra processing time for tanh and logistic versus ReLU is not V2's random-label versus true-label training-time comparison.

rows.subject: MLP implementation in scikit-learn
rows.size_stated: went deeper than one layer; exact configurations not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measured empirical capacity of deeper networks on randomly generated points and labelings.

conditions.value: small k and h in some cases

rows.measure: Empirical LM dimension / capacity compared with one-hidden-layer architecture
rows.value: There was no more than linear increase in the capacity; with small k and h, results were better by just one sample; in most cases LM dimension was far below empirical values of a respective network with one hidden layer.
rows.note: These are capacity results for deeper settings; exact per-configuration measurements are not stated.
rows.check: The depth comparison reports relative capacity without configurations, dataset sizes, or a stated stochastic optimizer. Lower capacity than a shallow network does not show failure to fit random labels in V1's setting.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: L-BFGS MLP capacity measurements on low-dimensional random points
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports fitting random labelings up to measured capacity, but does not test image-training error or chance test error (R1, R2). Some specially noted 2-hidden-node cases shattered only the stated sample counts (R2).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Adam/SGD or Keras settings described in the implementation comparison
reader_labels.reason: In most cases, these settings did not fit the data and had very low measured dimensions, so the result is sensitive to optimizer/implementation (R3).
